key_insight: Plasticity in layered inorganic semiconductors like GeSe is highly conditional, with deformation switching between sliding and brittle fracture depending on orientation, scale, and loading mode.
engineering_relevance: Design and screening for flexible electronics should use multi-direction, multi-scale mechanical testing rather than relying on a single compression or bending result.
method: Bending along the c-axis armchair direction
Micropillar compression with conventional and eccentric loading
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~23% strain without fracture under macroscopic compression, but brittle cleavage in bending and fragmentation in conventional micropillar tests, showing strongly divergent responses across evaluations.
watch_item: Apparent plasticity may be overestimated if test geometry, defect state, and stress path are not controlled consistently across experiments.
paper_title: Identifying Plastic Inorganic Semiconductors Requires More Rigorous Criteria
